definitions.gloss: to parade, to march in procession
definitions.explanation: To walk slowly and deliberately in a group through streets or an area, typically as part of a festival, celebration, or demonstration.

examples.japanese: {神輿|みこし}を{担|かつ}いで{町|まち}を{練|ね}り{歩|ある}く。
examples.english: They parade through town carrying the portable shrine.

examples.japanese: {仮装|かそう}した{人|ひと}たちが{通|とお}りを{練|ね}り{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: People in costumes paraded through the street.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{日|ひ}には{山車|だし}が{商店街|しょうてんがい}を{練|ね}り{歩|ある}き、{沿道|えんどう}の{観客|かんきゃく}がにぎやかに{声|こえ}を{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: On the festival day, floats paraded through the shopping street, and spectators along the route cheered loudly.

notes:
Godan verb ({五段動詞|ごだんどうし}), く-ending.
- Negative: {練|ね}り{歩|ある}かない
- Polite: {練|ね}り{歩|ある}きます
- Te-form: {練|ね}り{歩|ある}いて
- Past: {練|ね}り{歩|ある}いた

USAGE:
Often associated with festivals ({祭|まつ}り), processions, and demonstrations. The {練|ね}り component implies a slow, deliberate, stately movement rather than ordinary walking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {町|まち}を{練|ね}り{歩|ある}く: to parade through town
- {通|とお}りを{練|ね}り{歩|ある}く: to march along the street
- {神輿|みこし}を{担|かつ}いで{練|ね}り{歩|ある}く: to parade carrying a portable shrine
